To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
poor vision and not having an eyesight check are associated with low education, depression, and functional limitations.
poor vision is common in older people without a known eye condition, and is associated with other losses, including depression.
self-reported vision loss is associated with other losses of function, with low education, and with low number of chronic conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of older people at risk of poor vision, and with the identification of those at risk of failing to seek eye tests.
the identification of risk factors for self-reported poor vision, not with the accuracy of self-reported vision.

the need to identify those who are not accessing eye care, to understand why they do not access care, and to find effective strategies to increase the uptake of eye tests by those who may benefit from them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
self-reported poor vision is associated with other health problems, and that low educational attainment is associated with poor uptake of eye testing.
older people with low educational attainment are at increased risk of undiagnosed poor vision, and of not having had an appropriate eyesight check.
there is a need to improve the eye care of older people, especially in those who are socially deprived, have poor health literacy or are socially isolated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
older people who have poor vision, or who do not have an eye test, are likely to have other functional losses and may be more vulnerable to depression.
the health of older people is not just a matter of age but of a complex interaction of social, psychological and physical factors.
older people with low educational attainment, functional impairment, or with only one chronic condition are more likely to have poor self-reported vision or have not had a recent eye test.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk factors for having poor vision are different from the risk factors for not having had eye testing.
the risk factors we have identified may be used in primary care to target case finding for undetected vision loss.
there is a need for more research into barriers to uptake of eye tests among those with poor self-reported vision.
